daas-irab:141-141.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ﴾: a past verb and its object, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿مَعْرُوشاتٍ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَغَيْرَ﴾: a noun conjoined to معروشات; it is muḍāf, and ﴿مَعْرُوشاتٍ﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالنَّخْلَ وَالزَّرْعَ﴾: conjoined. ﴿مُخْتَلِفاً﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative. ﴿أُكُلُهُ﴾: the fāʿil (agent) of the active participle مختلف. ﴿وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالرُّمَّانَ﴾: conjoined. ﴿مُتَشابِهاً﴾: a ḥāl, accusative. ﴿وَغَيْرَ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined). ﴿مُتَشابِهٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿كُلُوا مِنْ ثَمَرِهِ﴾: an imperative verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذا﴾: a conditional adverb, non-jussive; the clause ﴿أَثْمَرَ﴾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَآتُوا﴾: an imperative verb like كلوا, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿حَقَّهُ﴾: its first object; its second object is omitted, its implied form being "the needy" (المحتاجين). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached to آتوا. ﴿حَصادِهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَلا تُسْرِفُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, and لا is negating; the clause ﴿لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ is the khabar of inna, and the clause إنه لا يحب المسرفين is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:142-142.t:
﴿وَمِنَ الْأَنْعامِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, its implied form being "and He created of the cattle". ﴿حَمُولَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the omitted verb.
﴿وَفَرْشاً﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كُلُوا مِمَّا﴾: an imperative verb to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached; it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, and the clause ﴿رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿خُطُواتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra. ﴿الشَّيْطانِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿عَدُوٌّ﴾: its khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from عدو: it was an adjective of it, and when it was placed before it, it became a ḥāl.
﴿مُبِينٌ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:143-143.t:
﴿ثَمانِيَةَ﴾: badal (substitute) from حمولة, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿أَزْواجٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنَ الضَّأْنِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from اثنين; it was an adjective of it before being placed ahead of it. ﴿اثْنَيْنِ﴾: badal from ثمانية. ﴿مِنَ الْمَعْزِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾: likewise. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) being "you" (أنت); the clause is resumptive. ﴿آلذَّكَرَيْنِ﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and الذكرين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed before the verb ﴿حَرَّمَ﴾.
﴿أَمِ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾: a conjoined noun, accusative with the yāʾ because it is dual; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أم﴾: a conjunction. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, conjoined to الأنثيين. ﴿اشْتَمَلَتْ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ are attached, and ﴿أَرْحامُ﴾ is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ. ﴿نَبِّئُونِي﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn because it is joined to the wāw of the plural; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is its object. ﴿بِعِلْمٍ﴾: attached to the verb before them; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive conditional particle. ﴿كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar (predicate). كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The conditional clause has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:144-144.t: ومن الإبل اثنين، ومن البقر اثنين …: the parsing of something similar was given in the previous verse. ﴿أَمِ﴾: a conjunction in the sense of بل ("rather, were you witnesses"). ﴿كُنْتُمْ شُهَداءَ﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar (predicate). ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb of time attached (mutaʿalliq) to شهداء. ﴿وَصَّاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهذا﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the kāf is its object and ﴿اللَّهُ﴾, the name of Majesty, its fāʿil (agent). The clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause كنتم is conjoined. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; من is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿أَظْلَمُ﴾ is its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّنِ﴾: attached to the elative noun (ism al-tafḍīl) أظلم. ﴿افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿لِيُضِلَّ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām, "for misleading"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb افترى, and the fāʿil is "he" (هو). ﴿النَّاسَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾: attached to افترى. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: inna, and the name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause ﴿لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ is its khabar; ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ is an adjective (ṣifa), accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause إن الله is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:145-145.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb. ﴿لا أَجِدُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil (agent) is "I" (أنا), and لا is negating, without governing effect. ﴿فِي ما﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb أجد.
﴿أُوحِيَ﴾: a passive past verb to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and ﴿مُحَرَّماً﴾ is its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The clause لا أجد is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). [Translator's note: as worded, «مفعوله» follows the gloss on أوحي; محرما is the object of أجد.] ﴿عَلى طاعِمٍ﴾: attached to the passive participle محرّم, and the clause ﴿يَطْعَمُهُ﴾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as an adjective (ṣifa) of محرّم. [Translator's note: so in the source; a genitive adjective here would qualify طاعم, not محرّم.] ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception. ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb); its noun is "it" (هو) and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿مَيْتَةً﴾. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb after it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَوْ دَماً مَسْفُوحاً أَوْ لَحْمَ﴾: conjoined. ﴿خِنزِيرٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ﴾: inna, its noun and its khabar; the fāʾ is for causation, and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿أَوْ فِسْقاً﴾: conjoined to لحم. ﴿أُهِلَّ﴾: a passive past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿بِهِ﴾ are attached; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); likewise the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿لِغَيْرِ﴾. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is in the position of accusative as an adjective. ﴿فَمَنِ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اضْطُرَّ﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil being "he" (هو). ﴿غَيْرَ﴾: a ḥāl, accusative. ﴿باغٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). ﴿وَلا عادٍ﴾: conjoined. ﴿فَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾: the fāʾ falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); inna, its noun and its two khabars; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive condition, and the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) with its apodosis is in the position of nominative as the khabar of من.

daas-irab:146-146.t:
﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb placed after, حرمنا. The clause after it, ﴿هادُوا﴾, is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿حَرَّمْنا﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كُلَّ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ذِي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is one of the five nouns.
﴿ظُفُرٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنَ الْبَقَرِ﴾: attached to حرّمنا. ﴿وَالْغَنَمِ﴾: conjoined. ﴿حَرَّمْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿شُحُومَهُما﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the hāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and mā is for the dual. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the excepted. ﴿حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُما﴾: the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَوِ الْحَوايا﴾: conjoined; and likewise ﴿أَوْ مَا اخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ﴾. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿جَزَيْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object.
﴿بِبَغْيِهِمْ﴾: attached to the verb before them; the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. The clause ذلك جزيناهم is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِنَّا لَصادِقُونَ﴾: inna, and نا is its noun, and صادقون its khabar, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).
The clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), after the wāw of ḥāl, or it is resumptive.

daas-irab:147-147.t:
﴿فَإِنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is a jussive conditional particle. ﴿كَذَّبُوكَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is resumptive.
﴿فَقُلْ﴾: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis. ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ذُو﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the wāw because it is one of the five nouns. ﴿رَحْمَةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿واسِعَةٍ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلا يُرَدُّ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative; لا is negating, without governing effect. ﴿بَأْسُهُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿عَنِ الْقَوْمِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to يرد. ﴿الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: an adjective, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ. The clause لا يرد is conjoined.

daas-irab:148-148.t: ﴿سَيَقُولُ﴾: an imperfect verb, the sīn being for the future; the relative noun ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿أَشْرَكُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; ﴿لَوْ﴾ is a non-jussive conditional particle; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). The clause ﴿ما أَشْرَكْنا﴾ has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and لا is negating. ﴿آباؤُنا﴾: conjoined to the pronoun نا in the verb أشركنا. ﴿وَلا حَرَّمْنا﴾: conjoined. ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾: من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; شيء is a noun genitive in form and accusative (manṣūb) in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause is conjoined to ما أشركنا. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: the kāf is a preposition and the demonstrative is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object): ﴿كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ "a denial being [like that]". The verbal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and a preposition; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the verb ﴿ذاقُوا﴾ and the an implied after حتى is in the position of genitive by the preposition: "until their tasting" ﴿بَأْسَنا﴾. [Translator's note: so in the source; an is not normally implied before a past verb after حتى.] ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle. ﴿عِنْدَكُمْ﴾: an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ﴾: من is a redundant preposition, and علم is a noun genitive in form and nominative (marfūʿ) in position as a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; the clause is the object of speech. ﴿فَتُخْرِجُوهُ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya); تخرجوه is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to what precedes it: "Is there with you knowledge, and so a bringing-out?" ﴿لَنا﴾: attached to the verb before them. ﴿إِنْ تَتَّبِعُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الظَّنَّ﴾: its object. ﴿إِنْ﴾: negating, without governing effect; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿تَخْرُصُونَ﴾ is its khabar; the clause وإن أنتم إلا تخرصون is conjoined.

daas-irab:149-149.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلِلَّهِ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it points to an implied condition: "if you have no proof, then to Allah belongs the conclusive proof". ﴿لله﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate): "the conclusive proof belongs to Allah". ﴿الْبالِغَةُ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿فَلَوْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿شاءَ﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿لَهَداكُمْ﴾: the lām falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); هداكم is a past verb and its object. ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾: tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

daas-irab:150-150.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative, its fāʿil (agent) being "you" (أنت). ﴿هَلُمَّ﴾: a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr) in the sense of "bring" (احضروا), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you (pl.)" (أنتم).
﴿شُهَداءَكُمُ﴾: its object; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as an adjective (ṣifa), and the clause ﴿يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: anna, and the name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause ﴿حَرَّمَ﴾ after it is its khabar (predicate), its fāʿil being "He" (هو). ﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna, its noun and its khabar is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by a preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb يشهدون, i.e. "to the forbidding of this". ﴿فَإِنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is a jussive conditional particle, and the past verb ﴿شَهِدُوا﴾ is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). [Translator's note: so in the source; شهدوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is فلا تشهد, as the next gloss states.] ﴿فَلا تَشْهَدْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive lā; the fāʾ connects the apodosis; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. ﴿مَعَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of place attached to the verb before it. ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; its fāʿil is "you" (أنت); the clause is conjoined. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: a conjoined relative noun. ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the verb. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِرَبِّهِمْ﴾: attached to the verb after them. ﴿يَعْدِلُونَ﴾: the clause is the khabar; the nominal clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:151-151.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَعالَوْا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَتْلُ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), by the dropping of the weak letter; the relative noun ﴿ما﴾ is its object. ﴿حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and ربكم is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا﴾: an is the accusative-governing particle; [تشركوا is] an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) from ما حرم, and لا is negating, without governing effect. ﴿وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ﴾: a noun, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is dual; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "do good" (تحسنوا). ﴿إِحْساناً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلادَكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and أولادكم its object. ﴿مِنْ إِمْلاقٍ﴾: attached to the verb before them; the clause is conjoined. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿نَرْزُقُكُمْ﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause نحن نرزقكم is causal (taʿlīliyya) or resumptive. ﴿وَإِيَّاهُمْ﴾: conjoined to the kāf in نرزقكم. ﴿لا تَقْرَبُوا الْفَواحِشَ﴾: لا is prohibitive, and [تقربوا is] an imperfect verb in the jussive, with its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ما ظَهَرَ مِنْها﴾: a past verb to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the relative noun ما is in the position of accusative as a badal from الفواحش, and the clause after it is its ṣila. ﴿وَما بَطَنَ﴾: conjoined. ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿الَّتِي﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as an adjective (ṣifa), and the clause ﴿حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). [Translator's note: the source writes ﴿أَلَّا﴾ here; the Quranic word is ﴿إِلَّا﴾.] ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in تقتلوا, i.e. "in the state of your being clothed with right". ﴿ذلِكُمْ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the kāf is its object and the mīm marks the plural; the clause is in the position of nominative as khabar. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾: laʿalla, and the kāf is its noun, and the clause تعقلون is in the position of nominative as its khabar. The clause لعلكم تعقلون is causal, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:152-152.t:
﴿وَلا تَقْرَبُوا﴾:
an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn because it is preceded by the prohibitive lā; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent), and ﴿مالَ الْيَتِيمِ﴾:
mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and اليتيم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا﴾:
a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِالَّتِي﴾:
attached (mutaʿalliq) to تقربوا. ﴿هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾:
mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿حَتَّى﴾:
a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿يَبْلُغَ﴾:
an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after حتى; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive by the preposition حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are likewise attached to the verb. ﴿أَشُدَّهُ﴾:
mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ﴾:
an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَالْمِيزانَ﴾:
conjoined to الكيل. ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾:
attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of أوفوا. ﴿لا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْساً﴾:
an imperfect verb and its object; لا is negating, without governing effect. ﴿إِلَّا﴾:
a particle of restriction. ﴿وُسْعَها﴾:
second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or parenthetical.
﴿وَإِذا﴾:
a conditional adverb, non-jussive; the clause ﴿قُلْتُمْ﴾:
is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَاعْدِلُوا﴾:
an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, and the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَلَوْ﴾:
the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿كانَ ذا﴾:
ذا is the khabar of kāna, accusative with the alif because it is one of the five nouns; the noun of kāna is omitted, its implied form being "the one judged against" (المحكوم عليه).
﴿قُرْبى﴾:
muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif. The clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿بِعَهْدِ﴾:
attached to the verb أوفوا after them; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾:
its counterpart has been given earlier.

daas-irab:153-153.t:
﴿وَأَنَّ هذا﴾: anna, and the demonstrative is its noun, and ﴿صِراطِي﴾ is its khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker.
﴿مُسْتَقِيماً﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb); the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَاتَّبِعُوهُ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; اتبعوه is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ its object; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا السُّبُلَ﴾: لا is prohibitive, and [تتبعوا is] an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm), with its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَتَفَرَّقَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya); its original form is تتفرق; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the maṣdariyya an and the verb is conjoined to an implied maṣdar preceding it, the implied form being: "let there be from you following and no scattering". ﴿بِكُمْ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl, the implied form being "taking you far away from His path". ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾: attached to the verb تفرق or to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكُمْ وَصَّاكُمْ بِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ﴾: its like has gone before.

daas-irab:154-154.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: conjunctive. ﴿آتَيْنا مُوسَى الْكِتابَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its two objects; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تَماماً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb), or ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عَلَى الَّذِي﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to تماما. ﴿أَحْسَنَ﴾: a past verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَتَفْصِيلًا﴾: conjoined to تماما. ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾: attached to تفصيلا. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً﴾: conjoined. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾: laʿalla and its noun, and the clause ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ is its khabar (predicate). ﴿بِلِقاءِ﴾: attached to the verb placed after, يؤمنون. The clause لعلهم بلقاء ربهم is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:155-155.t: ﴿وَهذا كِتابٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾: a past verb; نا is its fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ its object; the clause is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as a first adjective (ṣifa). ﴿مُبارَكٌ﴾: a second adjective. ﴿فَاتَّبِعُوهُ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; اتبعوه is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾: like اتبعوا; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾: laʿalla, and the kāf is its noun. ﴿تُرْحَمُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of laʿalla, and the clause لعلكم is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:156-156.t: ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām, the implied form being "lest you say" (لئلا تقولوا); it is also said to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the implied form being "out of dislike of your saying". The preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb أنزلناه. ﴿إِنَّما﴾: [inna] restrained [by mā] and the restraining [mā] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أُنْزِلَ الْكِتابُ﴾: a passive past verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عَلى طائِفَتَيْنِ﴾ are attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِنا﴾: attached to an adjective (ṣifa) of طائفتين. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); إن is lightened from the heavy [inna], without governing effect. ﴿كُنَّا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and نا is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as its noun. ﴿عَنْ دِراسَتِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar (predicate) ﴿لَغافِلِينَ﴾. The lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa) between the governing inna and the lightened, non-governing in; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:157-157.t: ﴿أَوْ تَقُولُوا﴾: conjoined to the first تقولوا. ﴿لَوْ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنَّا﴾: anna and its noun. ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾: a passive past verb to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and ﴿الْكِتابُ﴾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿لَكُنَّا أَهْدى﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar (predicate); the lām falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: attached to أهدى. The clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿فَقَدْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, the implied form being: "do not say that, for clear proof has come to you". ﴿جاءَكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the kāf is its object and بينة its fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition. ﴿وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾: conjoined. ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَظْلَمُ﴾: its khabar. ﴿مِمَّنْ﴾: a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by min; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أظلم. ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ are attached; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿وَصَدَفَ عَنْها﴾ is conjoined to it. ﴿سَنَجْزِي الَّذِينَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the relative noun is its object; the sīn is a particle of the future. ﴿يَصْدِفُونَ عَنْ آياتِنا﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿سُوءَ﴾: its second object. The clause is likewise the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position, and the clause سنجزي is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun particle), indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn. ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna, and the wāw is its noun, and the clause ﴿يَصْدِفُونَ﴾ is its khabar. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ما and the verb after it is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb نجزي, i.e. "We will requite them for their turning away from Our signs".

daas-irab:158-158.t:
﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle conveying negation. ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنْ﴾: accusative-governing. ﴿تَأْتِيَهُمُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb), and the hāʾ is its object. ﴿الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾: its fāʿil. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
Likewise أو يأتي ربك and ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ آياتِ رَبِّكَ﴾; the implied form is: "do they await anything but the coming of the angels, or the coming of your Lord…", etc. ﴿آياتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: the source prints ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾ with ḍamma; as muḍāf ilayhi it is the رَبِّكَ of آيات ربك.] ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb placed after, لا ينفع. ﴿لا يَنْفَعُ نَفْساً إِيمانُها﴾: لا is negating, and [ينفع is] an imperfect verb, with its object and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clause يأتي بعض is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, after the adverb يوم. ﴿لَمْ تَكُنْ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm), its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is in the position of accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of نفسا. ﴿آمَنَتْ﴾: a past verb, the tāʾ being for the feminine. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾: من is a preposition; قبل is an adverb of time, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because it is cut off from the iḍāfa; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them. The clause is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of تكن. ﴿أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِي إِيمانِها خَيْراً﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; خيرا is its object and the fāʿil is "she/it" (هي); the clause is conjoined. ﴿قُلِ﴾: an imperative verb; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿انْتَظِرُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنَّا﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿مُنْتَظِرُونَ﴾: its khabar. The clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:159-159.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the noun of inna. ﴿فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿وَكانُوا شِيَعاً﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَسْتَ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted khabar of laysa, and likewise the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿فِي شَيْءٍ﴾ are also attached to it. ﴿إِنَّما﴾: [inna] restrained [by mā] and the restraining [mā] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أَمْرُهُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb; the hāʾ is its object and its fāʿil is "He" (هو). ﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition. ﴿ما﴾: maṣdariyya (verbal-noun particle). ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna, and the wāw is its noun, and the clause ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ is its khabar. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ما and the verb is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb ينبئهم. The clause ينبئهم is conjoined.

daas-irab:160-160.t: ﴿مَنْ﴾: a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿جاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq). ﴿فَلَهُ﴾: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿عَشْرُ﴾: mubtadaʾ placed after. ﴿أَمْثالِها﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); the clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, and the clause of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) with its apodosis is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من. ﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ connects the apodosis; لا is negating. ﴿يُجْزى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو), and it is the first object. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مِثْلَها﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾: لا is negating; يظلمون is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of هم. The clause وهم لا يظلمون is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:161-161.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb. ﴿إِنَّنِي﴾: inna, and the yāʾ is its noun, and the nūn is for protection (wiqāya). ﴿هَدانِي﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif because it is impossible to pronounce; the nūn is for protection, and the yāʾ is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبِّي﴾: fāʿil (agent), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِلى صِراطٍ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb هداني. ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa); the clause إنني is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause هداني is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿دِيناً﴾: badal (substitute) from the position of إلى صراط, which is originally the second object of the verb هداني, because هدى takes its object directly, as in the words of Allah the Exalted ﴿اهْدِنَا الصِّراطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾, or through a preposition, as in this verse. ﴿قِيَماً﴾: an adjective of دينا. ﴿مِلَّةَ﴾: badal from دينا. ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa, a diptote because it is a proper name and non-Arabic. ﴿حَنِيفاً﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive; ما is negating. ﴿كانَ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar of kāna; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:162-162.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ صَلاتِي﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيايَ وَمَماتِي﴾: conjoined. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar (predicate). ﴿رَبِّ﴾: badal (substitute) from the name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural. The clause إن صلاتي is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

daas-irab:163-163.t: ﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation, which governs like inna. ﴿شَرِيكَ﴾: its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the overt fatḥa. ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted khabar (predicate) of lā; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَبِذلِكَ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; the bāʾ is a preposition; ذا is a demonstrative, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb placed after, ﴿أُمِرْتُ﴾. The lām is for distance and the kāf for address. The clause is conjoined. ﴿وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

daas-irab:164-164.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَغَيْرَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, accusative (manṣūb) with the fatḥa; the hamza is for interrogation. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَبْغِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness; the fāʿil (agent) is "I" (أنا). ﴿رَبًّا﴾: tamyīz (specification), accusative.
﴿وَهُوَ رَبُّ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause أبغي is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿كُلِّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا تَكْسِبُ كُلُّ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; لا is negating, without governing effect; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿عَلَيْها﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb تكسب. ﴿وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; لا is negating; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أُخْرى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra implied on the alif because it is impossible to pronounce. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: conjunctive. ﴿إِلى رَبِّكُمْ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ placed after, ﴿مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil being "He" (هو), and the kāf its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِما﴾: a relative noun in the position of genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: kāna, and the tāʾ is its noun. ﴿فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, to which the preposition and its genitive noun before it are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم. The clause كنتم is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:165-165.t: ﴿وَهُوَ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined. ﴿جَعَلَكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the kāf is its first object, and ﴿خَلائِفَ﴾ its second object. ﴿الْأَرْضِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). ﴿وَرَفَعَ﴾: a past verb to which the adverb ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq). ﴿بَعْضَكُمْ﴾: its object, and ﴿بَعْضٍ﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿دَرَجاتٍ﴾: accusative by removal of the preposition, [i.e.] "to degrees" (إلى درجات). ﴿لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the kāf is its object, its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb يبلوكم. [Translator's note: so in the source; the lām phrase is normally attached to the preceding verb (رفع or جعل), not to يبلوكم itself.] ﴿فِي ما﴾: ما is a relative noun in the genitive; [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to the verb. ﴿آتاكُمْ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the kāf is its object and the fāʿil is "He" (هو); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ الْعِقابِ﴾: inna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ is conjoined.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ﴾: you put kasra on the alif of (أنّ) and on the one after it in its jawāb (apodosis), as a fresh start (iʾtināf), and that is in the reading of the Readers.
And if you wish, you put fatḥa on the alif of (أنّ), meaning: your Lord has written upon Himself that whoever does…
And for the (أنّ) that comes after the fāʾ you have both kasra and fatḥa. As for the one who reads it with fatḥa, he says: the writing (al-kitāb) needs (أنّ) only once; but the predicate (khabar) is its proper place, so when it entered at the beginning of the speech it was repeated in its proper place; as He said: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ﴾: since the position of أنّ is "does he promise you that you will be brought forth when you have died", it entered at the beginning of the speech and at its end. Similar to it is: ﴿كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنّهُ مَـنْ تَوَلاَّهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ﴾ with fatḥa. And similar to it is: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّهُ مَنْ يُحَادِدِ اللّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَأَنّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾. And you may put kasra on the (إن) that comes after the fāʾ in these passages, as a resumption (istiʾnāf); do you not see that you would find it good to say: "كتب أنه من تولاه فهو يضله" ("It was written that whoever takes him as an ally, he leads him astray") with fatḥa [Translator's note: i.e. with fatḥa on the first أنه]. Likewise "وأصلح فهو غفور رحيم" ("and makes amends, then He is Forgiving, Merciful"), if it were so, it would be correct. So whenever the insertion of (هو) is good, the kasra is good.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِيَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾: you put (السبيل) in the nominative by His saying (وليستبين), because the verb belongs to it. Whoever treats السبيل as feminine says: ﴿وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾. And the verb may be made to belong to the Prophet ﷺ, so you put السبيل in the accusative, the meaning being: "and that you, O Muhammad, may make clear the way of the criminals (ولتستبين يا محمد سبيلّ المجرمين)".

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلاَّ للَّهِ يَقُصُّ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾: it was written with the yāʾ dropped because it meets the alif and lām [Translator's note: i.e. the reading يقضِ الحقّ, written without yāʾ]; just as ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانيَةَ﴾ was written without wāw, and as ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾ was written without yāʾ, following the pronunciation. This is the reading of the companions of ʿAbdallāh [ibn Masʿūd]. And it is reported from ʿAlī that he read: (يَقُصُّ الْحَقَّ) with ṣād. He said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, he said: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated to me from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from a man from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read (يقضِى بالحق). Al-Farrāʾ said: and so it is in the reading of ʿAbdallāh.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ حَبَّةٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: it is permissible to put it in the nominative (rafʿ).

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ مَن يُنَجِّيكُمْ مِّن ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً﴾: one says خُفيَة and خِفية. And there is a dialect form of it with wāw — not valid in recitation —: خُفوة and خِفوة; just as it is said: "he untied his ḥubwa (حُبْوته), ḥibwa (حِبوته) and ḥibya (حِبْيته)".
His saying: ﴿لَّئِنْ أَنجَانَا مِنْ هَـٰذِهِ﴾ is the reading of the people of Kufa — and so it is in their codices —: "أن ج ى ن ألف" [Translator's note: i.e. spelled with a yāʾ, nūn and alif: أنجينا]; some of them read with the alif (أنجانا), and the reading of the people at large is (أنجيتنا) with tāʾ.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱلْقَادِرُ عَلَىٰ أَن يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَاباً﴾: as He did to the people of Noah: the rain, the stones and the flood. ﴿أَوْ مِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾: the swallowing up by the earth (al-khasf). ﴿أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً﴾: He mixes you up into factions (shiyaʿ) of differing whims.

farraa:69-69.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن ذِكْرَىٰ﴾ is in the position of the accusative or the nominative; [the accusative] by an implied (muḍmar) verb: (ولكِن) we remind them a (ذِكرى) reminding; and the nominative on the reading: (ولكن) it is (ذكرى) a reminder.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿وَذَرِ الَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَهُمْ لَعِباً وَلَهْواً﴾: it is said: there is no people but that they have a feast, and they amuse themselves at their feasts, except the community of Muhammad ﷺ; for their feasts are piety, prayer, takbīr and good.
His saying: ﴿وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ أَن تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ﴾ means: [lest a soul] be held in pledge. (The Arabs say: "هذا عليك بَسْل", i.e. this is forbidden to you. And for that reason it is said "أسَد باسل", i.e. a lion that is not to be approached.) And the Arabs say: "أعْطِ الراقِىَ بُسْلته" ("give the charmer his busla"), which is the fee for the charm.

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq and his wife were calling their son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān to Islam. That is His saying: ﴿إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾, i.e. obey us. And if it were "إِلى الهدى أن ائتنا" it would be correct; as He said: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحاً إِلَى قَوْمِهِ أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ﴾, in many similar cases, where أَنْ is sometimes brought and sometimes dropped.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنْ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلاةَ...﴾ is referred back (maʿṭūf) to the lām in His saying: ﴿وأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ﴾. The Arabs say: "أمرتك لتذهب" ("I commanded you that you go"), (and "وأن تذهب"); so أَن is in the position of the accusative by being referred back to the command. And there is much like it in the Qurʾān.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾: it is said that His saying (فيكون) refers specifically to the Trumpet (al-ṣūr), i.e. He says to the Trumpet: (كُنْ فَيَكُونُ).
And it is said that His saying (كن فيكون) belongs with His saying "His word is the truth (هو الحقّ)", as a naʿt (description) of the word; then you make its verb ﴿يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾, meaning: His word will be the truth on that day. And it may be that you say: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾ of every thing, so that it is a self-sufficient phrase, and you put "the word (القول)" in the nominative by "the truth (الحقّ)", and put (اليوم) in the accusative because it is the setting (maḥall) for "His word is the truth".
The Arabs say: نِفخ فى الصورِ and نُفِخَ; and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (كهيئة الطير فأنفخها فتكون طيرا بإذنى). And the poet said:
لولا ابنُ جَعْدة لم يُفتَح قُهُنْدُزكم * ولا خُراسانُ حتى يُنْفَخَ الصورُ
(Were it not for Ibn Jaʿda, your citadel would not have been opened, nor Khurāsān, until the Trumpet is blown.)
And it is said that al-ṣūr is a horn; and it is said: it is a plural of ṣūra (form), the blowing into the forms (al-ṣuwar) being into the dead.
And Allah knows best what is correct in that.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ آزَرَ﴾: it is said: آزر is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), and it does not take tanwīn (lā yujrā) because it is foreign (aʿjamī). The genealogists are agreed that he was the son of Tāraḥ, so it is as though Āzar was a nickname for him. And it has reached me that the meaning of (آزر) in their language is "crooked", as though he reproached him for his deviation and crookedness from the truth. Some of them read (لأبيه ازرُ) in the nominative, as a vocative (with يا), and that is a good reading. His saying: ﴿أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَاماً آلِهَةً﴾: you put the idols in the accusative because the verb falls upon them.

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ﴾: one says جنّ عليه الليل and أَجَنَّ, and أَجنَّه الليل and جَنّه الليل; with the alif is better when you drop (على), and it is more common than جنَّه الليل.
Two views are given on His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ رَأَى كَوْكَباً قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَبِّي﴾: that he said "this is my Lord" only to draw his people step by step towards the proof against them, in order to reproach their gods as being nothing, and that the star, the moon and the sun were greater than them and yet were not gods; and it is said: he said it in the other sense; as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوَى. وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالاّ فَهَدَى﴾; and here they adduced as proof Abraham's saying: ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ يَهْدِنى رَبِّى لأَكُونَنّ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الضَّالِّينَ﴾.

farraa:100-100.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ﴾: if you wish you may make ﴿الجِنّ﴾ an explanation of "partners". And if you wish you may make its accusative be on [the meaning]: they made the jinn partners to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.
His saying: ﴿وَخَرَقُواْ﴾: and اخترقوا, خلقوا and اختلقوا, meaning: they fabricated.

farraa:102-102.t: His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمُ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لاۤ إِلَـٰهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾: ﴿خَالِقُ﴾ is put in the nominative as a new start (ibtidāʾ), or as being a khabar (predicate). If you put it in the accusative, since it has no alif and lām, by way of qaṭʿ (cutting off), it would be correct; it is like His saying: ﴿غَافِرِ الذَّنْبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِ﴾, and likewise: ﴿فَاطِرِ السَّمَوَاتِ والأَرْضِ﴾ — if you put it in the accusative when there is a complete definite noun before it, that would be permissible; for you may say: "الفاطر السموات", "الخالق كل شىء", "القابل التوب", "الشديد العقاب". And you may say: "مررت بعبد الله محدِّثِ زيد" ("I passed by ʿAbdallāh, the one who talks with Zayd"), making it definite even though alif and lām would fit it well, when he has become known by that; so it is like your saying: "مررت بوحشىّ قاتل حمزة" ("I passed by Waḥshī, the slayer of Ḥamza"), and "بابن ملجَم قاتِل علىّ" ("by Ibn Muljam, the slayer of ʿAlī"): he became known by it until it became like a name for him.

farraa:105-105.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلآيَاتِ وَلِيَقُولُواْ دَرَسْتَ﴾: they say: you learned from the Jews. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (وليقولوا درس), meaning Muhammad ﷺ. It is as you say in speech: "قالوا لى: أساء" ("they said to me: he did wrong") and "قالوا لى: أسأت" ("…you did wrong"). Similar to it: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَيُغْلَبُونَ﴾ and ﴿سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾.
Some read (دارست), meaning: you disputed with the Jews and they disputed with you; and so said Ibn ʿAbbās. Mujāhid read it (دارَسْت) and explained it: you read to the Jews and they read to you.
And it has been read (دُرِسَتْ), i.e. it was read and recited. And they read (دَرُسَتْ) and they read (دَرَسَتْ), meaning: it has grown old, i.e. this that he recites to us is something that has lasted long and passed by us.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَآ آتَيْنَاهَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ﴾: that is because they said to him: "Do you not fear that our gods will strike you with madness for your reviling them?" So he said to them: "Do you not fear that yourselves from them, since you have made equal the small and the great, the male and the female — that the great one will be angry since you have made the small one equal to it?" Then he said to them: "Is the one who worships one god more entitled to be safe, or the one who worships scattered gods?" They said: "The one who worships one god", and so they became angry with themselves. That is His saying: ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَآ آتَيْنَاهَآ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ﴾.

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ﴾: this hāʾ is for Noah: and (We guided) of his offspring David and Solomon. If David and Solomon were put in the nominative on this meaning, since the verb is not overt, it would be correct; just as you say: "أخذت صدقاتِهِم لكل مائة (شاةٍ شاةً) وشاةٌ" ("I took their alms: for every hundred sheep, one sheep"), [with شاة in the accusative] and [in the nominative] شاةٌ.

farraa:86-86.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْيَسَعَ﴾: the companions of ʿAbdallāh double the lām [Translator's note: i.e. read وَاللَّيْسَع], and that is more like the foreign names than [the reading of] those who say (والْيَسَعَ); the Arabs hardly ever put alif and lām on what does not take tanwīn (mā lā yujrā), such as Yazīd and Yaʿmur, except in poetry; one of them recited:
وَجَدْنا الوليد بن اليزيد مباركا * شديدا بأَحْنَاء الخِلافةِ كاهِله
(We found al-Walīd son of al-Yazīd blessed, his shoulders strong to bear the burdens of the caliphate.)
He put the alif and lām on Yazīd only because he had put them on al-Walīd. And when the Arabs do that, they give the word a touch of praise.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿فَإِن يَكْفُرْ بِهَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾ means the people of Mecca; ﴿فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنَا بِهَا قَوْماً﴾ means the people of Medina; ﴿لَّيْسُواْ بِهَا بِكَافِرِينَ﴾ — [disbelieving] in the sign (al-āya).

farraa:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾: they did not magnify Him as He truly should be magnified. His saying ﴿تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَرَاطِيسَ﴾: He says: how could you say "Allah has not sent down anything to a human being", when the Torah was sent down to Moses ﴿تَجْعَلُونَهُ قَرَاطِيسَ﴾; and al-qirṭās in this place is a sheet. Likewise His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَاباً فى قِرْطَاسٍ﴾ means: on a sheet.
﴿تُبْدُونَهَا وَتُخْفُونَ كَثِيراً﴾: He says: you show what you like, and you conceal the description of Muhammad ﷺ.
His saying: ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾: Muhammad ﷺ was commanded to say ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾, i.e. Allah sent it down to you. And if you wish you may say: say: (He is) Allah.
And His saying ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾ may be an answer to His saying: ﴿مَنْ أَنزَلَ ٱلْكِتَابَ ٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِهِ مُوسَىٰ﴾ — ﴿قُلِ ٱللَّهُ﴾ sent it down. I chose putting ﴿ٱللَّهُ﴾ in the nominative not as an answer only because it is Allah, Blessed and Exalted, who commanded Muhammad ﷺ to ask them: ﴿مَنْ أَنزَلَ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾, and it is not a question from them so that they would be answered; but it is permissible because it is a question, and a question may have an answer.
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ ذَرْهُمْ فِي خَوْضِهِمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾: if it were in the jussive (jazm) it would be correct; as He said: ﴿ذَرْهُمْ يأكُلُوا وَيَتَمتّعُوا﴾.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِتُنذِرَ أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ﴾: it is said in the exegesis that the Mother of Towns (umm al-qurā) is Mecca.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾: the hāʾ may refer to Muhammad ﷺ or to the Revelation.

farraa:93-93.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾: it is said that it was revealed concerning Musaylima the Liar, and that is because he claimed prophethood.
﴿وَمَن قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ﴾: and مَن is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ). He means: and who is more wrongful than this one and than this one who said: "I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down." It was revealed concerning ʿAbdallāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ.
That is because he used to write for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when the Prophet ﷺ said: ﴿وَاللّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمُ﴾ he would write (سميع عليم) or (عزيزحكيم), and the Prophet ﷺ would say to him: "It is the same"; until he dictated to him His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الإنْسَانَ مِنْ سُلاَلَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقاً آخَرَ﴾, and Ibn Abī Sarḥ said ﴿فَتَبَارَكَ اللّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ﴾, in wonder at the detailing of the creation of man. He said: and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Thus was it sent down to me", so he doubted and apostatised. And he said: "If Muhammad ﷺ is truthful, then it has been revealed to me (as it was revealed to him), and if he is lying, then I have said the like of what he said." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down concerning him: ﴿وَمَن قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنَزلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ بَاسِطُوۤاْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: and it is said: stretching out their hands to draw out the souls of the disbelievers. It is like His saying: ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ﴾. If it were (باسطون), it would be (أيدِيَهُمْ) [in the accusative]; and if it were "باسطو أيديهم أن أخرِجوا" it would be correct. Similar to it, among cases where أن is left out, is His saying: ﴿يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى الْهدَى ائْتِنَا﴾. And when you drop (أن) from speech like this, a verb of saying is implied (muḍmar) in it, as in His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ تـَرَى إِذِ المُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهِمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — they say: ﴿رَبَّنا﴾.

farraa:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا فُرَادَىٰ﴾: it is a plural. The Arabs say: [a people] فرادى and فرادُ, O you, and they do not give it tanwīn (lā yujrūnahā), likening it to ثُلاَث and رُبَاع. The singular of فرادى is فَرْد, فرِد and فريد; and فراد is for the plural, and فرد is not permissible in this sense. One of them recited to me:
ترى النُعَراتِ الزُرْق تحت لَبَانه * فُرَادَ ومثنى أصعقتها صواهِله
(You see the blue gadflies beneath his breast, singly and in pairs, struck down by his neighing.)
His saying: ﴿لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: Ḥamza and Mujāhid read (بينُكُمْ), meaning "your bond". And in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (لقد تقطع ما بينَكم), and that is the natural form of the speech. When the verb is made to belong to بين it is left in the accusative; just as they say: "أتانى دونك من الرجال" ("there came to me men below you"), leaving it in the accusative although it is in the position of the nominative, because it is a description (ṣifa). And when they say: "هذا دون من الرجال" ("this is an inferior one among men") they put it in the nominative in the nominative position. Likewise you say: "بين الرجلين بين بعيد" and "بون بعيد" ("between the two men is a great gap"); when you use it on its own you give it tanwīn in Arabic and give it the case inflection (iʿrāb).

farraa:96-96.t:
His saying: ﴿فَالِقُ ٱلإِصْبَاحِ﴾: al-iṣbāḥ is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "أصبحنا إصباحا" ("we entered the morning"), and al-aṣbāḥ is the morning of each day, collectively.
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ ٱلْلَّيْلَ سَكَناً وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ حُسْبَاناً﴾: الليل is in the position of the accusative in meaning. So He referred the sun and the moon back to its meaning, since He separated between them by His saying (سكنا); and when you do not separate them by anything, they prefer the genitive. And the accusative is permissible even if nothing comes between them; one of them recited:
وبينا نحن ننظره أتانا * معلِّقَ شَكْوةٍ وزِنادَ راع
(While we were watching for him, he came to us, hanging up a water-skin and a shepherd's fire-stick.)
And you say: "أنت آخذٌ حقَّك وحَقِّ غيرك" ("you are taking your right and the right of others"), putting the second in a genitive construct while you gave tanwīn to the first; because the meaning of your saying "أنت ضارب زيدا" and "ضاربُ زيدٍ" is the same. The best of this is that you put something between them; as Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فظلّ طُهاة اللحم من بينِ مُنْضِج * صفيفَ شِواءٍ أو قَدِيرٍ معجَّلِ
(And the cooks of the meat kept on, some ripening a row of roast, or a hastened pot-stew.)
So he put الصفيف in the accusative and القَدِير in the genitive, according to what I told you.

farraa:98-98.t: His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾ means in the womb, ﴿وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾ in the man's loins. And it is read (فمستقِرّ), meaning the child in the womb, (ومستودع) in the man's loins. Its nominative is by implying a description (ṣifa) [Translator's note: i.e. an implied predicate such as "of them"]; as when you say: "رأيت الرجلين عاقل وأحمق" ("I saw the two men: a wise one and a fool"), meaning: of them is such and such.

farraa:109-109.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾: those swearing are the disbelievers. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to bring them the sign that was revealed in al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾; so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to have it sent down and swore that they would believe. The believers said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask your Lord to send it down upon them so that they believe." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: Say to those who believe: "And what makes you perceive that they will believe?" This is the reason for the accusative [fatḥa] in أنّ: "and what makes you perceive that they will believe", (and) We ﴿نُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ كَمَا لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾. Some read: (إنها) with kasra on the alif, (إذَا جَاءَتْ) as a fresh start, and make His saying (وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ) a self-sufficient statement. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is: (وما يشعِركم إذا جاءتهم أنهم لا يؤمنون).
And (لا) in this place is a ṣila (redundant connective); like His saying: ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلَى قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: the meaning is: it is forbidden to them that they return. And similar to it: ﴿مَا مَنَعَكَ أَنْ لاَ تَسْجُدَ﴾, its meaning is: that you prostrate.
In the reading of Ubayy it is: (لعلها إِذا جاءتهم لا يؤمِنون). The Arabs have a usage for (لعلّ) in that they say: "ما أدرى أنك صاحبها" ("I do not know — perhaps you are the one"), meaning: لعلك صاحبها; and they say: "ما أدرى لو أنك صاحبها"; and it is a good interpretation to make (أنّ) stand in the place of لعل.

farraa:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَآ إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةَ﴾: this is a thing they had asked for, so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: if We did that for them they would not believe ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
His saying: (قُبُلاً) is the plural of qabīl, and al-qabīl is the guarantor (al-kafīl). I chose here that al-qubul should be in the sense of guaranteeing only because of their saying: ﴿أَوْ تَأتِى بِاللّهِ وَالْمَلاَئِكَةِ قَبِيلاً﴾ — guaranteeing that. And (قُبُلا) may mean: from before their faces; as you say: "I came to you from the front (قُبُلا) and did not come to you from behind (دُبُرا)". And al-qabīl may be a plural of qabīla (tribe), as though you said: or you bring us Allah and the angels tribe by tribe and group by group. And if it were read قَبَلا in the sense of "face to face (muʿāyanatan)" it would be correct, as you say: "أنا لقيته قبلا" ("I met him face to face").

farraa:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نِبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً شَيَاطِينَ ٱلإِنْسِ وَٱلْجِنِّ﴾: you put "enemy" and "devils" in the accusative by His saying: جعلنا.
His saying: ﴿يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ﴾: Iblīs — according to what is mentioned — assigned one party of his devils to humans and one party to the jinn; when the devil of the human and the devil of the jinnī meet, [the first] says: "I led my companion astray with such and such, so lead your companion astray with it", and (the devil of the jinnī) says the like of that to him. This is their inspiring one another. Al-Farrāʾ said: Ḥayyān narrated that to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās.

farraa:113-113.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِيَقْتَرِفُواْ مَا هُم مُّقْتَرِفُونَ﴾: al-iqtirāf is earning; the Arabs say: "So-and-so went out to earn (yaqtarif) for his family."

farraa:114-114.t: His saying: ﴿مُنَزَّلٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾: of those who doubt that they know that it is sent down from your Lord.

farraa:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾ in eating carrion, ﴿يُضِلُّوكَ﴾, because most of them were astray. That is because they said to the Muslims: "Do you eat what you have killed and not eat what your Lord has killed!" So this verse was sent down: ﴿وَإِن تُطِعْ أَكْثَرَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.

farraa:117-117.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مَن يَضِلُّ﴾: (من) is in the position of the nominative, like His saying: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أىُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَى﴾. When (من) comes after [verbs of] knowing, looking and perceiving — such as نظرت, علمت and دريت — it follows the pattern of أىّ. If after it there is a verb whose agent it is, you put it in the nominative by that verb; and if after it there is a verb that falls upon it, you put it in the accusative; as when you say: "ما أدرى من قام" ("I do not know who stood"), you put (من) in the nominative by قام; and "ما أدرى من ضربت" ("I do not know whom you struck"), you put it in the accusative by ضربت.

farraa:120-120.t: His saying: ﴿وَذَرُواْ ظَاهِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ﴾: as for its outward part, it is debauchery and fornication; and as for its inward part, it is secret companionship (al-mukhālla): that the woman takes a lover and that he takes her.

farraa:121-121.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ﴾: He says: your eating that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned is fisq, i.e. disbelief. He alluded to the eating [by the pronoun], as He said: ﴿فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَاناً﴾, meaning: the people's saying increased them in faith.

farraa:122-122.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَ مَن كَانَ مَيْتاً فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ﴾: i.e. he was astray and We guided him.
His saying: ﴿نُوراً يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ means his faith.

farraa:124-124.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُواْ صَغَارٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. from Allah; so said the exegetes. And in Arabic it is as you say: "سيأتينى رزق عندك" ("provision with you will come to me"), like your saying: "سيأتينى الذى عند الله" ("what is with Allah will come to me"): the humiliation that is with Him will strike them, and it is for Muhammad ﷺ to bring it down on them. But it is not permissible in Arabic to say "جئت عند زيد" while you mean "from Zayd (من عند زيد)".
And His saying ﴿صَغَارٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ may mean that they chose disbelief out of pride and disdain for following Muhammad ﷺ, so Allah made that humiliation in His sight.

farraa:125-125.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَن يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلاَمِ وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ﴾: [مَن] and مَن are in the position of the nominative by the hāʾ that refers back to each of them.
His saying: (يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقاً حَرِجاً): Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿUmar read it (حرِجا), and the people read it حَرَجا. Al-ḥaraj — according to Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation — is a place thick with trees which the grazing flock cannot reach. He said: likewise the breast of the disbeliever, wisdom cannot reach it. With kasra and with fatḥa it is like waḥad and waḥid, farad and farid, danaf and danif: the Arabs say them with one meaning.
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾: He says: the way became narrow for him, and he found nothing but to climb into the sky, and he is not able. And it is read (كأنما يصَّاعَد), meaning يتصاعد, and (ويَصْعد) without doubling.

farraa:128-128.t: His saying: ﴿يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ قَدِ ٱسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ﴾: He says: you have led many astray. His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ أَوْلِيَآؤُهُم مِّنَ ٱلإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا ٱسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنَا بِبَعْضٍ﴾: the humans' enjoyment of the jinn is that a man, when he went off alone and felt lonely, or killed one of their game and became afraid, would say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley", and would spend the night feeling safe. As for the jinn's enjoyment of humans, it is the reverence from humans that they obtained through them; the jinn used to say: "We have become lords of the jinn and the humans."

farraa:130-130.t:
His saying: ﴿يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنْكُمْ﴾: someone may say: the messengers are from humans only, so how did He say to the jinn and the humans (منكم) "from among you"? It is said: this is like His saying: ﴿مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيَانِ﴾, then He said: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ﴾, whereas pearls and coral come out only from the salt water and not from the fresh.
So it is as though you said: they come out from part of them, from one of them.

farraa:131-131.t:
His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكَ أَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ رَّبُّكَ﴾: if you wish you may make (ذلك) in the position of the accusative, and make (أن) one of those where a genitive-governing preposition fits, so that when you drop it, it is accusative. He means: He did that because [your Lord] was not one to destroy the towns.
And if you wish you may make (ذلك) nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf), since the verb is not overt. Similar to it: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ﴾ and ﴿ذَلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾. And similar to it: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِيَعْلَمَ أَنِّى لَمْ أَخُنْهُ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ and ﴿ذَلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللّهُ مُوهِنُ كَيْد الْكَافِرِينَ﴾: the nominative and the accusative are permissible in all of it.
His saying: ﴿مُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا غَافِلُونَ﴾: He says: He was not one to destroy them for their wrongdoing while they are heedless, no messenger nor proof having yet come to them. And His saying in Hūd: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ الْقُرَى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ﴾: He says: He was not one to destroy them for their wrongdoing, i.e. for their associating partners [with Allah], (while their people are doing right), dealing with each other justly among themselves. Thus the exegesis has come. And there is another sense in it — and it is dearer to me than this, because associating partners [with Allah] is the greatest of sins — and the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: He was not one to destroy them by wrongdoing on His part while they are doing right.

farraa:99-99.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾: He says: the provision of every thing, meaning what grows and is fit as nourishment for every thing. Thus the exegesis has come, and it is the natural sense of the speech. In Arabic it is also permissible that you put "vegetation" in a genitive construct with "every thing" while by "every thing" you also mean the vegetation, so that it is like His saying: ﴿إنّ هَذَا لَهُوَ حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ﴾, where al-yaqīn is the ḥaqq itself. His saying: ﴿مِنَ النَّخْلِ مِنْ طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ﴾: the proper form is the nominative for القنوان, because the meaning is: and from the palm trees, their clusters are near. If it were put in the accusative — "and He brought out from the palm trees, from their spathes, near clusters (قنوانا دانية)" — it would be permissible in speech, but it is not recited so because of the written text.
His saying: ﴿وَجَنَّاتٍ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ﴾ is accusative, except that the feminine plural with tāʾ takes the genitive ending in the position of the accusative; and if you put الجنات in the nominative following القنوان, it would be correct.
His saying: ﴿وَفِى الأَرضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِرَاتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ﴾: the proper form there is the nominative, making it follow القطع; and if you put it in the accusative and made it follow الرواسى and الأنهار, it would be correct.
His saying: ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ﴾ means the olive tree and the pomegranate trees, just as He said: ﴿وَاسْأَلَ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning the people of the town.
His saying: ﴿ٱنْظُرُوۤاْ إِلِىٰ ثَمَرِهِ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ﴾: He says: look at it when it first sets fruit, (وَيَنْعِهِ): its ripening. And it has been read (ويُنْعِهِ) and (ويانِعِهِ). As for His saying: ﴿ويُنْـعِهِ﴾, it is like "its ripeness (نضجه)", and يانعه is like "its ripe and mature state (ناضجه وبالغه)".

farraa:135-135.t:
His saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ﴾: (مَنْ تَكُونُ لَهُ) is in the position of the nominative; and if you put it in the accusative it would be correct; as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وَاللّهُ يَعْلَمُ المُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ﴾.
His saying: ﴿مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ﴾: when the subject of the verb is feminine and of the nature of a maṣdar (verbal noun), such as al-ʿāqiba (outcome), al-mawʿiẓa (admonition) and al-ʿāfiya (well-being), then when you put its verb before it you may make the verb feminine or masculine; as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿فَمَنْ جَاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾ with the masculine, and said: ﴿قَدْ جَاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ with the feminine. Likewise ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ and ﴿وَأَخَذَتِ﴾. So do not shy away from either masculine or feminine in this.
[Translator's note: the source literally says "when the verb (al-fiʿl) is feminine"; al-Farrāʾ means the noun that the verb is predicated of.]

farraa:136-136.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا للَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ﴾, and برُعْمِهم and زِعمِهم: three dialect forms [Translator's note: the source writes برُعْمِهم with rāʾ, evidently for بزُعْمِهم]. No one we know of has read it with kasra on the zāy. The Arabs sometimes treat a word thus in cases like this; they say: al-fatk, al-futk and al-fitk, and al-wudd, al-widd and al-wadd, among similar words. The best of it is what the Readers from whom recitation is transmitted have chosen. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "وهذا لشركائِهم"; and it is as you say in speech: ʿAbdallāh said: "he has wealth (إنّ له مالا)" and "I have wealth (إنّ لى مالا)", meaning himself. And the poet said:
رَجْلانِ من ضَبّة أَخبرانا * إنا رأينا رجلا عريانا
(Two men of Ḍabba informed us: "We saw a naked man.")
And if he had said "they informed us that they had seen" it would be correct.

farraa:137-137.t:
His saying: ﴿ٰلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلاَدِهِمْ شُرَكَآؤُهُمْ﴾: they were a people who served their gods, and they made burying daughters alive seem fair to them. Also, one of them would say: "If such-and-such a number of males is born to me, I will sacrifice one of them." That is the killing of their children. And الشركاء is nominative, because they are the ones who made it seem fair.
Some used to read: "وكذلك زُيِّن لِكثِيرٍ مِن المشركين قتلُ أولادِهم", putting القتل in the nominative since its agent is not named, and putting (الشركاء) in the nominative by a verb he intends; as though he said: their partners made it seem fair to them. Similar to it is His saying: (يُسَبَّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالآصَالِ), then He said: ﴿رجَالٌ لاَ تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ﴾. In some of the codices of the people of Syria it is (شركايهم) with yāʾ; if that is established from the early ones, then it ought to be read (زُيِّنَ), and the partners would be the children, because they share with them in lineage and inheritance. But if they read (زَيَّنَ), I do not know its rationale; unless in it they were following the dialect of a people who say "أتيتها عِشايا" and then say in the dual of (الحمراء: حمرايان); this would be a way for them to have said: "زَيَّنَ لكثيرٍ من المشركين قتل أولادِهم شركايُهُمْ". And if you wish, when you read (زَيَّنَ) with fatḥa, you may make it a verb of Iblīs and then put الشركاء in the genitive as following الأولاد. The view of whoever said that they intended something like the poet's saying:
فزججتها متمكّنا * زجَّ القَلوصَ أبِى مزاد
(I thrust her firmly, as Abū Mazād thrusts the young she-camel.)
is worth nothing. This is among what the grammarians of the people of the Ḥijāz used to say, and we have not found its like in Arabic.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation is cut in the source as ﴿ٰلِكَ﴾, i.e. ﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ﴾; the poetic verse illustrates separating muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi by the object, the construction attributed to the Syrian reading زُيِّنَ … قتلُ أولادَهم شركائِهم.]

farraa:139-139.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ خَالِصَةٌ لِّذُكُورِنَا﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is "خالص لذكورنا". Its being feminine is because of the femininity of الأنعام; since what is in their bellies is like them, it was made feminine because of their femininity. Whoever makes it masculine does so because (ما) is masculine. Some have read "خالصُهُ لذكورِنا", putting it in a genitive construct with the hāʾ, the hāʾ referring to ما. And you could put الخالص and الخالصة in the accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off), making the predicate of ما lie in the lām in His saying (لِذُكُورِنَا), as though you said: what is in the bellies of these cattle is for our males, exclusively (خالصا / خالصةً), as He said: ﴿وَلَهُ الدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾. But the accusative in this position is rare; they hardly say "عبدالله قائما فيها" ("ʿAbdallāh, standing, is in it"), but it is analogically sound.
His saying: ﴿وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً فَهُمْ فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ﴾: if you wish you may put الميتة in the nominative, and if you wish you may put it in the accusative, saying (ميتةً). And you may say تكن or يكن, with tāʾ or yāʾ.
And al-khāliṣa may be a maṣdar, given its feminine form, as you say al-ʿāqiba and al-ʿāfiya. It is like His saying: ﴿إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ﴾.

farraa:141-141.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ مَّعْرُوشَاتٍ وَغَيْرَ مَعْرُوشَاتٍ﴾: these are the vines. Then He said: ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُتَشَابِهاً﴾ in its colour, and ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ﴾ in its taste: some of it sweet and some of it sour.
His saying: ﴿وَآتُواْ حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ﴾: this is for the orphans and the poor who are present at it.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ﴾: in giving all of it. That is because Thābit ibn Qays left the people free to take from his palm trees, and all of it was taken and nothing of it remained for his family; so Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ إِنَّهُ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾.

farraa:142-142.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً﴾: He says: and He produced for you from the cattle beasts of burden (ḥamūla), meaning those able to carry and work; and al-farsh: the small ones.

farraa:143-143.t:
His saying: ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: if you wish you may make "eight" referred back (as badal) to الحمولة; and if you wish you may imply a verb for it.
His saying: ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾: the male is a pair-member (zawj) and the female is a zawj. And if you put "two and two" in the nominative because of the entry of (مِن), it would be correct, as you say: "رأيت القوم منهم قاعد ومنهم قائم" ("I saw the people: of them is one sitting and of them one standing"), and [also] قاعد وقائما.
The meaning of His saying: ﴿قُلْ ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ﴾: He says: did the prohibition come to you, in what you have forbidden of the sāʾiba, the baḥīra, the waṣīla and the ḥām, from the two males or from the two females? If they said: "from the side of the male", every male would be forbidden to them; and if they said: "from the side of the female", every female would be forbidden to them.
Then He said: ﴿أَمَّا ٱشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ﴾: He says: or has He forbidden you what the womb contains? If they said that, male and female would be forbidden to them, because the womb contains both male and female. And (ما) in His saying "أمّا اشْتَمَلَتْ" is in the position of the accusative; you put it in the accusative as following the two males and the two females.

farraa:144-144.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآءَ﴾: He says: did Allah enjoin this on you, you seeing it with your own eyes?

farraa:145-145.t:
His saying: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَجِدُ فِي مَآ أُوْحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً﴾, then He, Majestic is His Face, said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً﴾; and if you wish, (تَكُونَ). In (الميتة) there are two possibilities: the nominative and the accusative. The nominative is not valid in recitation, because الدم is in the accusative by being referred back to الميتة, and it [i.e. أو دما] has an alif that prevents the nominative from being permissible. And (أن تكون) is permissible because الميتة is feminine, then you refer what comes after it back to it. Whoever puts (الميتة) in the nominative makes it the fiʿl of (يكون) [Translator's note: al-Farrāʾ's term; here: its subject], content with يكون without a predicate. Likewise (يكون) in all exception constructions does not need a predicate; do you not see that you say: "ذهب الناس إلا أن يكون أخاك" and "أخوك" ("the people went, unless it be your brother")? Kāna and yakūn could do without a predicate only as what follows إلا does without a verb belonging to the noun. Since it is said "قام الناس إلا زيدا" and "إلا زيد", putting it in the accusative without a verb and in the nominative without a verb, kāna was fit to be complete (tāmma).
